review: 1:1 אוֹר שָׁמַיִם — the Arabic repeats نُورٌ سَمَاوِيّ twice; Hebrew repeats the same two words so the acclamation stays an acclamation and does not become a sentence.
1:4 הוֹי שִׂמְחָתִי — 'O my joy', for يَا لَسُرُورِي; the Arabic لَام of exclamation has no Hebrew equivalent, and הוֹי carries the exclamation without turning into a lament.
2:1 הֹלֵךְ אָנִי — the participle plus pronoun keeps the Arabic's 'walking' as a durative, which a finite verb would lose.
3:2 לֹא יַסְתִּירוּ פְּנֵי דוֹדִי — 'they shall not hide my Beloved's face'; the Arabic لَا تَحْجُبَنَّ takes the cares and pains as subject, and Hebrew keeps the plural verb for the same reason.
4:2 הַפְּרָס — 'the prize' (1 Cor 9:24, βραβεῖον); the Arabic الْمُجَازَاة is 'recompense', and פְּרָס is the fixed Hebrew term for the runner's prize.
